description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='2022-07-19' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-YY' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. This program opens no file and is reached by no JCL, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57, the arm literal at L142 and the group move at L122, never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here: no Language Environment CEE* service exists in this environment, so CEEDAYS cannot be called at all. Arm 7 of the ten-arm EVALUATE at L128-L149: FC-BAD-PIC-STRING, 88-level VALUE X'000309D659C3C5C5' (L68), whose two leading halfwords DECODE to severity 0x0003 = 3 and message number 0x09D6 = 2518. Both numbers are read out of that hex rather than interpolated from the neighbouring arms, which matters because the nine tokens are not consecutive - 0x09D7, which would be 2519, is absent from the set entirely. Arm 7 is reached here by a second and quite different route from case15's. In case15 the mask contains a letter that begins no recognised token; here every character is a legitimate token, and the fault is that the YEAR role is declared TWICE, once as YYYY and once as YY. A parser that only rejected unknown letters would accept this mask and then silently prefer one of the two years. The duplicate-role rejection is taken while the picture string is still being scanned, so it precedes the completeness check applied once scanning ends: this mask also carries no day field at all, and had the duplicate not been caught first the outcome would have been 2507 for insufficient data instead of 2518. Pinning that precedence is the whole point of the case. It also proves tokens are matched greedily and longest-first, since a parser that read YYYY as two YY fields would reject case01's mask as a duplicate too. The date itself is the well-formed one from case01, and WS-DATE still reports it, because L122 overwrites the clean copy made at L107-L108 with a GROUP move whose leftmost two bytes are the Vstring-length halfword 0x000A set from LENGTH OF LS-DATE at L105 - so only the first eight characters, '2022-07-', survive into PIC X(10) and the trailing '19' is discarded. WS-DATE-FMT is set at L111-L113 and is not a target of L122, so the mask is echoed clean and this case therefore shows the message being assembled from both parameters even when only one of them is at fault.
